resourceProfile.assessment: The complete English and Danish source scope, review metadata, glossary, and project concept references were available locally.

automatedQuality.summary: Translation review metadata, queue validation, typecheck, 79 test files with 462 tests, complete build, 39 IIS rules with 61 route cases, and 724 generated-link checks passed.

linguisticCritique.summary: A bounded Danish pass identified 25 actionable formula, terminology, grammar, and English-residue defects across electrical, circuit, trigonometric, thermal, unit, and wire-gauge content; all 25 were corrected.

competentHumanReview.summary: No competent Danish human review was performed in this cycle; changed IDs remain machine-drafted.

publicationAuthorization.summary: No merge, publication, deployment, or residual-risk authorization was requested or granted.

findings.summary: The current formula omitted spacing around division.
evidence: The previous expression was ‘I = V/R’.
findings.resolution: Restored ‘I = V / R’.

findings.summary: The resistance formula omitted spacing around equality and division.
evidence: The previous expression was ‘R = V/I’.
findings.resolution: Restored ‘R = V / I’.

findings.summary: The unit-conversion instruction omitted the definite article.
evidence: The previous instruction was ‘Hold enheder konsistente før beregning’.
findings.resolution: Changed it to natural Danish ‘Hold enhederne konsistente før beregningen’.

findings.summary: The Joule example described a power rate as joules per second without stating the equivalent power.
evidence: The previous conclusion said the coil converts energy at ‘7,2 joule pr. sekund’.
findings.resolution: Clarified the result as 7.2 W or 72 J over 10 seconds.

findings.summary: The heat-transfer bullet retained the English loanword hardware.
evidence: The previous bullet used ‘hardware’.
findings.resolution: Changed it to the Danish term udstyr.

findings.summary: The circuit glossary used the English term node.
evidence: The previous bullet began ‘En node er ...’.
findings.resolution: Changed it to the Danish electrical term knude.

findings.summary: The series-connection definition used an awkward literal construction for current flow.
evidence: The previous bullet said ‘giver strøm kun én vej’.
findings.resolution: Rephrased it as the series connection carrying current only one way.

findings.summary: The parallel-cell bullet used an awkward passive phrase for summed capacity.
evidence: The previous bullet ended with ‘tilføjes ca.’.
findings.resolution: Rewrote it as capacity and available current being approximately added together.

findings.summary: The sine formula used the abbreviated modsat label rather than the definite Danish side term.
evidence: The previous expression was ‘sin(θ) = modsat / hypotenusen’.
findings.resolution: Changed it to ‘den modstående / hypotenusen’.

findings.summary: The tangent formula used inconsistent abbreviated side labels.
evidence: The previous expression was ‘tan(θ) = modsat / tilstødende’.
findings.resolution: Standardized it to ‘den modstående / den tilstødende’.

findings.summary: The inverse-cosine formula used the English hypotenuse label.
evidence: The previous expression ended with ‘/ hypotenuse’.
findings.resolution: Changed it to the Danish definite form hypotenusen.

findings.summary: The inverse-tangent formula mixed abbreviated and definite Danish labels.
evidence: The previous expression used ‘modsat / tilstødende’.
findings.resolution: Standardized it to ‘den modstående / den tilstødende’.

findings.summary: The TCR current formula omitted spacing around division.
evidence: The previous expression was ‘I = V/R’.
findings.resolution: Restored ‘I = V / R’.

findings.summary: The heat-capacity example used the wrong grammatical gender for varmelegeme and an incomplete loss phrase.
evidence: The previous conclusion said ‘en rigtig varmelegeme ... på grund af tab’.
findings.resolution: Changed it to ‘et rigtigt varmelegeme’ and clarified heat loss.

findings.summary: The heating-time conclusion spelled out the protected seconds unit.
evidence: The previous conclusion ended with ‘523 sekunder’.
findings.resolution: Restored the concise protected notation 523 s.

findings.summary: The phase-change limitation used a vague specific-heat reference.
evidence: The previous paragraph referred only to ‘specifik varme’.
findings.resolution: Changed it to the precise term specifikke varmekapacitet.

findings.summary: The heat-flux definition used the older loanword after the title had been localized.
evidence: The previous paragraph repeatedly used ‘varmeflux’.
findings.resolution: Aligned the paragraph with the preferred Danish term varmestrømstæthed.

findings.summary: The heat-flux summary used an imprecise literal rate phrase.
evidence: The previous summary described the ‘satsen’ of heat transfer.
findings.resolution: Changed it to the clear phrase ‘Hastigheden for varmeoverførsel pr. arealenhed’.

findings.summary: The conduction note used the generic English-derived word flow.
evidence: The previous bullet said ‘angiver flow’.
findings.resolution: Changed it to the Danish technical term varmestrøm.

findings.summary: The imperial-unit paragraph retained English names for inches and their squared/cubed forms.
evidence: The previous paragraph used ‘inches, square inches og cubic inches’.
findings.resolution: Translated the unit names to tommer, kvadrattommer, and kubiktommer.

findings.summary: The length-conversion formulas retained English unit names and decimal points.
evidence: The previous formulas used inch, foot, feet, and decimal points.
findings.resolution: Localized the unit names and normalized Danish decimal commas across the formula set.

findings.summary: The gauge-number bullet used the awkward phrase måler 0.
evidence: The previous correction still said ‘størrelser over måler 0’.
findings.resolution: Changed it to the clearer Danish phrase måletrinnet 0.

findings.summary: The wire-gauge comparison retained the awkward phrase strandede konstruktion.
evidence: The previous paragraph used ‘strandet konstruktion’.
findings.resolution: Changed it to the natural Danish phrase flertrådet konstruktion.

findings.summary: The stranded-wire instruction used the English-derived strengkonstruktion.
evidence: The previous bullet used ‘strengkonstruktion’.
findings.resolution: Changed it to trådkonstruktionen.

findings.summary: The final wire-gauge instruction used the vague phrase aktuelle kapacitet.
evidence: The previous bullet said ‘Bestem den aktuelle kapacitet’.
findings.resolution: Changed it to the precise term strømkapaciteten.
